title: Docs site writing and code-snippet standards
author: Priya Menon
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page defines the team-wide conventions, validation rules, and release procedures for all documentation prose and embedded code snippets on the Redwood docs site. The goal is consistent, secure, and runnable examples that reduce developer friction and support maintainability across SDKs, CLI examples, and API reference pages.

Scope
- Applies to all public and internal doc pages under eng-developer-experience (quickstarts, API examples, SDK guides, and docs-site operations).
- Does NOT replace language-specific style guides (e.g., PEP8) but augments them with examples and interop conventions tailored to Redwood APIs.

Key principles
1) Trustworthy and runnable: prefer examples that a reader can run locally with minimal setup.
2) Secure by default: snippets must never contain secrets or customer data. Use placeholders and environment variable patterns.
3) Multi-language parity: canonical examples should exist for Python and JavaScript at minimum; where relevant include Go and curl.
4) Short and focused: examples should demonstrate a single concept or API surface per snippet.

Snippet metadata and storage
- Central snippet registry: all reusable snippets must be stored in the docs-snippets repository and referenced by snippet ID. Do not inline large multi-file examples directly in the Confluence page.
- Snippet ID format: docs-snippet::<area>::<short-name>::v<major> (example: docs-snippet::sdk::basic-generate::v1)
- Each snippet entry must include a metadata header (YAML or JSON) with fields: id, title, languages (list), requires (list of env vars/packages), test_command, last_tested_at, owner.

Required snippet metadata table (example)
| Field | Meaning | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| id | canonical snippet identifier | docs-snippet::api::text-gen::v1 |
| languages | languages maintained in repo | python, javascript |
| requires | environment/runtime requirements | REDWOOD_API_KEY, python>=3.10 |
| test_command | command used by CI to validate snippet | pytest tests/snippets/test_text_gen.py |
| owner | team or person responsible | eng-developer-experience |

Formatting and content rules
- Language tags: always include a language tag in fenced code blocks (```python, ```bash).
- CLI and curl examples: place curl examples in a dedicated "curl" block and prefer --fail-with-body for better error visibility. Use placeholders for endpoints and tokens: e.g. -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY".
- Environment variables: prefer $UPPER_SNAKE_CASE placeholders and document how to set them locally (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...).
- Timeouts and limits: include explicit timeout parameters for network calls in examples where applicable (e.g., timeout=10).
- Output trimming: when showing generated text output, include a "// truncated" comment for long outputs and show token counts where useful.

Example: minimal Python generation (canonical)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient  # canonical import path
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='redwood-2-small', prompt='Write a haiku about latency', max_tokens=60, timeout=10)
print(resp.text)
```

Example: equivalent curl (canonical)
```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","prompt":"Write a haiku about latency","max_tokens":60}' 
```

Security and redaction rules
- Never hardcode API keys, tenant IDs, customer PII, or internal hostnames. Use environment variables or placeholder tokens (e.g., <REDACTED_KEY>).
- If an example needs to show an obfuscated identifier, use redwood-test-0000-style IDs.
- For any page that formerly contained a secret, open an incident ticket and rotate credentials immediately; include the incident ID in the doc change log.

Testing and CI integration
- All snippets referenced from the docs site must have an automated smoke test in docs-snippets/tests/ with a short runtime (<= 60s). Tests should be idempotent and use recorded responses or mocked endpoints unless exercising live-hosted features that are explicitly labeled as live-demo.
- CI job names: docs:snippets:validate and docs:snippets:lang-compat (runs language matrix: python, node). Failures block the docs release pipeline.
- Required badge: pages that include live-run snippets must bear a "Live-run tested" badge with last_tested_at metadata visible.

Localization and accessibility considerations
- Keep code comments and inline prose concise to reduce translation burden. Avoid idioms that do not translate well.
- Strings meant for translation: wrap UI text used in examples with double quotes and list them under a "localizable_strings" key in the snippet metadata.
- Accessibility: ensure images for code screenshots include ALT text and images are accompanied by the equivalent runnable snippet.

Procedure: adding or updating a canonical snippet
1) Author creates/updates files in docs-snippets with metadata and tests.
2) Open a PR against docs-snippets with the snippet ID in the title. Tag reviewers: @eng-developer-experience and language owners (python, js).
3) CI runs tests and language matrix. Address failures.
4) Once CI passes, create or update the Confluence page referencing the snippet ID. Include a short explanation and expected output.
5) Reviewer signs off on the page content and the snippet owner merges both changes.
6) During release windows, the docs-release pipeline picks validated snippets and publishes pages.

Rollback and hotfix guidance
- If a snippet introduces a breaking change (e.g., API surface change or credential leak), revert to the previous snippet ID version (e.g., v1 -> v0) and open an incident.
- For urgent fixes to public pages, use the emergency docs patch flow: PR -> tag release-team -> deploy partial fix with a short banner on the page noting the change and reason.

Common support patterns and canonical fixes
- Top snippet-related support asks: auth errors in examples, mismatched language parameter names, and outdated model names. Maintain a small canonical fixes registry in the docs-snippets repo with quick patches for each common failure.
- Example canonical fix entry: auth-error-mismatch-headers: explanation, affected-pages, fix-commit-id.

Ownership and maintenance cadence
- Owners: eng-developer-experience maintains the canonical snippet registry. Language owners (Python SDK, JS SDK) are responsible for language parity and test maintenance.
- Review cadence: every 3 months perform a snippet audit for top-50 pages and update last_tested_at. Major model or API changes trigger an immediate audit.

Appendix: snippet validation checklist (author)
- [ ] Snippet has metadata and ID in docs-snippets repo.
- [ ] Tests present and passing locally.
- [ ] No secrets present; placeholders used.
- [ ] Language tags applied to fenced code blocks.
- [ ] Example output trimmed and annotated where necessary.
- [ ] Reviewer assigned and CI green.

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: eng-developer-experience Slack #devx-docs and ping @PriyaMenon for ownership questions.
- For live-demo outages or credential issues escalate to security on-call and open a PagerDuty incident.

Change log

- 2024-11-14: added CI job names, snippet ID format, and localization guidance (reviewed by Ethan Cole).
- 2025-11-02: clarified testing timeout guidance and added rollback flow (reviewed by Marta Alvarez).
